chapter: Working with Duke and final reflections
title: Starting to copy for Duke after the Apollo closed
summary: Whaley lost his Apollo job in 1940, Duke called wanting a copyist, and Duke trusted him to change parts that sounded wrong.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Well, Tom what I want to know now is how did you start to write for Duke now? Score and orchestrate for him?

Listen -- see, I was in the Apollo Theatre, and the girls -- this was in 1940, and the girls wanted more money, see, and the man wouldn't give them any money, so they quit. And that took me out of a job, see. See, I used to arrange and copy all my music and rehearse it for the band, see, and when the girls quit, I quit with them because I didn't have no job, see?
So in '40, Duke called me and I thought I was going to be an arranger, see, and he wanted a copyist. I said okay, I'd copy.
And that's how I started copying with Duke.
How did you get to add the parts, like you were saying Sam Wooding had you add trumpets to his parts -- Duke would say to you, Tom, write this part. How did that happen?
How did Duke trust you with his music and say you orchestrate it the way you know I want it?
Oh, I don't know. I used to write, and if something didn't sound good to me, I'd change it.
Oh, there's a whole lot of things that went on.
